concerns.text: Piecewise linear regression (pwlf) is applied to the binary task‑level success outcome. PLR assumes a continuous response with homoscedastic errors; using it on a Bernoulli variable violates model assumptions and yields an unreliable breakpoint estimate.

The breakpoint validation compares the sparse‑grid breakpoint to a dense‑grid estimate derived from the same task‑level data (bootstrap CI vs. dense‑grid estimate). This is a circular validation because both estimates are functions of the identical predictor‑outcome pairs, providing no independent evidence of a true tipping point.

VIF is calculated for ‘library_size’ and ‘total_redundancy’, yet total redundancy is a deterministic function of library size (and the fixed overlap level). The two predictors are not independent, so VIF does not meaningfully assess collinearity and may be misleading.

The plan does not include a statistical test to evaluate whether the change in slope at the estimated breakpoint is significant. Because PLR will always produce a breakpoint, the claim of a “tipping point” may be a trivial artifact rather than an empirically supported finding.
